# Gap fill: repeats, caps, escalation, habituation, Kao 2020

Scope: gaps (a) to (e) from `p5-p6-p7-juice-repeat-sound.md` Part 6. Field framework names used as given: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition; windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

Headline: the gap is mostly NOT closed. No named studio VFX talk with muzzle-flash variant counts, random ranges, or combo step sizes was reachable. Best new numbers come from adjacent sources (sound design, mobile VFX budget, engine budget). Each is labelled.

## 1. Search count used

15/15 WebSearch. About 28 WebFetch (many failed, listed below).

## 3. Gap-by-gap results

### GAP: (a) How many variants an every-second effect needs

Status: PARTLY FILLED (sound and authoring counts only; no VFX studio talk number)

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sound designer practice: footsteps and sword swings, about ten near-identical variations [V: confirmed - article dated 16 May 2018, byline Asbjoern Andersen, text by Bjorn Jacobsen] | ~10 variants for the most frequent sounds | industry practice (Jacobsen 2018, sound, pre-2020) | G6 |
| Doors: 5 variants per layer; layering multiplies: 5 per layer gave 125 combinations, 625 with an optional sweetener [V: confirmed] | 5 per layer, 125 / 625 combos | industry practice (Jacobsen 2018) | G6 |
| Explosions: moved from 3 size-based variations to layered sounds giving "hundreds" of combinations [V: confirmed] | 3 -> hundreds | industry practice (Jacobsen 2018) | G6 |
| Layering beats stacking raw variants: combine small sets of independent layers to get many combinations | transfer to VFX = inference. A muzzle flash of 3 core shapes x 3 smoke x 2 spark sets = 18 looks from 8 assets (my arithmetic) | inference | G6 |
| Halo 3 (talk 2008): over 30 weapons each needed a muzzle flash [V: confirmed]. Team rejected one tinted bitmap (quality) and rejected dozens of unique flashes (effects budget) [V: unverified - reasons for the two rejections not re-seen in the fetch summary]. Chose one grey flash texture plus a 1x256 colour texture [V: confirmed] | no per-weapon variant count given | industry practice (Bungie 2008, pre-2020) | G4 |
| Destiny 2: "avoid flipbooks" [V: confirmed - page says they do not use flip books]; mix and match a shared texture library, multiply two textures with different tile rates and UV scroll so the player cannot tell which masks are used | qualitative; no count | industry practice (Stavrides, Bungie, via 80 Level) | G5 |
| Random varied feedback in a controlled study: enjoyment +.11 (p<.05), no curiosity effect (already in first run) | Non-varied = a single effect; varied = random pick per trigger. Variant count not stated in text I read | study | G2 |
| Authoring count for a random flipbook segment: about 16 frames usually enough (tier C, single source, carried from first run, not re-opened) | 16 frames | industry practice, tier C, needs second source | first-run S12 |

What is still missing: a named studio number for muzzle flash, footstep dust, coin pickup or impact variants. Not found in 15 searches.

| VFX variant count for every-second effects (muzzle flash, dust, coin, impact) | STILL OPEN | Studio: fire effect at 1 per second for 100 shots with 1, 3, 6 variants; owner marks the shot where it reads as a repeat. Log chosen counts per effect class |
